items.title: John LaPorta interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: But there was something prophetic in the liner notes that Nat Hentoff wrote

ctx.x: Did you have aspirations as a classical clarinetist?

Well I did then, and I got more and more involved with the jazz end of it, and it seemed just too difficult for me to try to keep up both things, especially at that time. Because Wynton Marsalis made a liar out of me you know, because he’s done beautifully at both of them. I did record the Brahms Sonata for Clarinet, that was quite a few years ago. I was under exclusive contract with Fantasy and I thought one of my projects each year would be to do a serious work, by serious I mean classical work, and then do…
